Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of novel stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids.
description: Amended Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids. Novel psychoactive substances (NPS) in the illegal drug supply pose risks to Canadians. However, little is known about their pharmacological activity. More potent drugs increase the risk of overdose risks. Evidence on the pharmacological activity of these substances is essential to support scientific regulatory activities and risk assessments. The illegal drug supply is continuously evolving, with new substances continually being detected. There is a need for further information on their harms to Canadians. This procurement activity will allow for the evaluation of the in vitro pharmacological activity of two categories of emerging drugs: synthetic cannabinoids, and stimulants. The data generated from this contract will inform future assessment activities and allow the OLRA to make more informed regulatory science decisions. For both streams, they require the pharmacological testing of different classes of substances, and require acquisition of reference standards and control samples, getting licenses for controlled substances, conducting experiments (including doing statistical analysis), and finally drafting and finalizing reports. Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide Pharmacological Testing for Stimulants, and Synthetic Cannabinoids in two (2) separate streams to Health Canada. Stream 2 – In vitro pharmacological testing of novel synthetic cannabinoids and Stream 3 – In vitro pharmacological testing of stimulant compounds. Each stream will be evaluated separately, and bidders are to provide their submissions for one (1) stream or two (2) streams. Up to two (2) contracts may be awarded under this amended request for proposal.

description: 35,000# Base Capacity 4-Wheel Sit-Down AC Electric Lift TruckHeavy-Capacity Battery-Electric ForkliftQuantity: 1 eachDelivery Location: McAlester Army Ammunition Plant Warehouse 8 C Tree RdMcAlester, OK 74501Required Delivery Date: Before or No Later Than September 30th, 2027.Delivery Terms: FOB Destination.1. RequirementThe Government requires the purchase and delivery of quantity 1 each, new heavy-capacity, battery-electric, counterbalanced forklift(s) for indoor industrial material-handling operations.The offered equipment shall be new, current production, and meet or exceed every minimum salient characteristic below. Used, refurbished, remanufactured, prototype, or demonstrator equipment is not acceptable.A manufacturer name, brand, or model number is not required. Offerors may propose any make or model that meets all stated requirements.2. Minimum Salient CharacteristicsNo. Characteristic Minimum Requirement2.1 Equipment type Four-wheel, sit-down, counterbalanced, battery-electric forklift suitable for heavy industrial material handling. AC Drive and Lift System.2.2 Electrical system Battery-electric propulsion and lift system. The system shall provide performance equal to or better than a 72-volt electrical system. Shall have transistor control technology.2.3 Rated capacity The forklift shall have a rated lifting capacity of not less than 28,700 pounds at a 24-inch load center and at a maximum fork height of 103.5 inches, with the furnished forks and fork-positioner attachment installed. Free Lift 0.0 inch with standard Load Backrest.2.4 Capacity data plate The delivered forklift shall have a legible manufacturer capacity/data plate identifying the rated capacity for the furnished mast, forks, and attachment configuration.2.5 Mast Two-stage mast, or functionally equivalent high visibility heavy duty mast rails configuration, capable of a maximum fork height of not less than 103.5 inches.2.6 Lowered mast height Overall lowered mast height shall not exceed 112.7 inches.2.7 Overhead guard height Overhead guard height shall not exceed 102.56 inches.2.8 Mast tilt Mast shall provide at least 6 degrees forward tilt and 7 degrees rearward tilt.2.9 Carriage Pin-type carriage, or functionally equivalent carriage, compatible with the furnished fork positioner. Nominal carriage width shall be 62 inches.2.10 Forks Furnish one pair of forks with minimum dimensions of 3.5 inches thick x 7 inches wide x 72 inches long. Forks shall be compatible with the furnished carriage and rated for the forklift/attachment configuration.2.11 Fork positioner Furnish an integral sideshifting fork positioner Pin Type (includes 4-way Valve and 3rd and 4th Function Hosing), nominal width 62 inches, capable of both sideshift and fork-positioning functions.2.12 Hydraulic functions Furnish all valves, controls, hydraulic lines, hoses, fittings, and other equipment required for complete operation of the fork-positioner and sideshift functions.2.13 Tires Cushion tires, sized and load-rated by the manufacturer for the offered forklifts rated capacity and intended indoor operating surface with front tires: 28 inches x 16 inches x 22 inches (Cushion) and rear tires: 22 inches x 10 inches x 16 inches (Cushion).2.14 Steering Full hydraulic power steering or functionally equivalent power steering with tilt steering column.2.15 Travel speed Travel speed shall be not less than 4.8 miles per hour.2.16 Lift speed Lift speed shall be not less than 32 feet per minute.2.17 Operator-presence protection Furnish an operator-presence sensing system or equivalent safety interlock that prevents unintended vehicle movement or hydraulic operation when the operator is not properly positioned.2.18 Braking Furnish a service-brake system and hand-actuated parking brake, or functionally equivalent parking-brake system.2.19 Warning devices Furnish, at a minimum: (a) audible reverse alarm; (b) amber warning beacon/strobe; and (c) rear-facing blue warning light or equivalent visibility warning device.2.20 Rear visibility Furnish rear camera system or functionally equivalent rear-visibility aid.2.21 Lighting Furnish forward work light(s) and rear combination light(s) suitable for normal indoor industrial operations.2.22 Operator display Furnish an integrated operator display that includes, at a minimum, an hour meter and system-status information.2.23 Battery compartment Forklift shall accommodate a battery compartment approximately 40 inches long x 60 inches wide, open-top configuration, or an equivalent configuration compatible with the offered forklift and required duty cycle.2.24 Battery and charger Not included.2.25 Warranty complete forklift Furnish a minimum warranty of 12 months or 2,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first, covering the complete forklift.2.26 Warranty powertrain Furnish a minimum powertrain warranty of 36 months or 6,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first.2.27 Manuals Furnish one electronic and one hard-copy operators manual, maintenance manual, parts manual, and warranty documentation for each forklift.2.28 Delivery condition Deliver forklifts fully assembled, serviced, inspected, and ready for operation.2.29 Operator orientation Provide on-site operator familiarization/orientation for Government personnel at time of delivery. Training shall address normal operation, safety features, charging requirements, daily inspection requirements, and basic preventive-maintenance actions.2.30 Compliance The offered equipment shall comply with all applicable Federal, state, and local requirements for powered industrial trucks and workplace safety.2.31 Additional Equipment Mechanical controls, Vinyl Semi-Susp. Seat, Operator Pres. Sens. The RLP is available through the Leasing Portal at: https://leasing.gsa.gov/leasing/s/ViewRLP The U.S. Government is seeking competitive lease proposals for new and/or continuing leasing opportunities through the Leasing Portal. Award under this RLP will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offer, without negotiations. City: Portland/South Portland State: Maine Delineated Area: Within a mile outside or within the boundaries defined below. Southern Boundary- Pinepoint Road to Broadturn Road to Burnham Road Western Boundary- Burnham Road to ME-22 to Saco St to Bracken Road to Libby Avenue to Main St Northern Boundary- Main St to ME-25 to Conant Street to William Clark Drive to New Gorham Road to Main Street to Bridge Street to East Bridge Street to Forest Avenue to Brook Street to Brook Road to Leighton Road to Falmouth Road to Middle Road to Johnson Road to Town Landing Road Eastern Boundary- Maine Coastline (Black line) Minimum ABOA Square Feet: 2,305 Maximum ABOA Square Feet: 2,397 Space Type: Office or flex space Parking: 13 surface (reserved) Lease Term: 15 Years / 13 Firm Amortization Term: 8 years for both Tenant Improvements and Building Specific Amortized Capital. Offerors are encouraged to submit rates for all terms available in the AAAP RLP to be considered for future requirements. AGENCY UNIQUE REQUIREMENTS Agency Tenant Improvement Allowance: New leased space: $71.54 per ABOA SF Building Specific Amortized Capital (BSAC): New leased space: $25.00 per ABOA SF Additional Requirements: The offered space must be contiguous yielding 2,305 - 2,397 USF. Ground floor preferable; The offered space must be located no less than 400 feet from the nearest school, licensed daycare facility, playground, public park, or place of worship, as measured from the nearest property line of the offered building to the nearest property line of the listed facility types. Surface level parking with efficient vehicular ingress and egress with convenient access to both I-95 and I-295. The agency must have 24 hour/7 days a week access to building and parking. Post Award Schedule: Attached to this advertisement/notice is the post award schedule for this project. It replaces the attachment referenced in section 1.05 of the RLP (R100) and should be used when reviewing section 4.01 of the Lease (L100). HOW TO OFFER The Leasing Portal (https://leasing.gsa.gov) enables interested parties to offer space to the Federal Government through a secure, web-based process. To participate, register on the site by selecting �Register to Offer Space� and follow the instructions provided. Helpful resources�including instructional guides and video tutorials�are available on the portal under the Resources tab. The Open Period runs from the 1st through the 7th of each month, ending at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time unless otherwise stated by the Government and unless the 7th falls on a weekend or Federal Holiday. If the 7th falls on a weekend or Federal Holiday, the Open Period will end at 8:00 PM (ET) on the next business day. No submissions are accepted during the Closed Period. During an Open Period, users may submit new offers, or modify or withdraw existing ones. Lease awards will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offer without negotiations. Offered space must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local jurisdiction requirements, including standards for fire and life safety, accessibility, seismic resilience, and energy efficiency. IMPORTANT NOTES Check the attachments and links section of this notice for possible, additional project-specific requirements or modifications to the RLP. Please review Section 889 of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) regarding telecommunications equipment restrictions: https://acquisition.gov/FAR-Case-2019-009/889_Part_B SAM registration should be initiated as soon as possible. Refer to RLP Section 3.06, subparagraph B.7 The Government may award multiple leases to satisfy new requirements or to compete expiring leases. Specific requirements will be identified following the close of the Open Period. Subleases will not be considered. title: 35K lb. Base Capacity 4-wheel Sit-Down AC Electric Lift Truck, including Options, Battery, Charger, and Freight
description: 35,000# Base Capacity 4-Wheel Sit-Down AC Electric Lift TruckHeavy-Capacity Battery-Electric ForkliftQuantity: 1 eachDelivery Location: McAlester Army Ammunition Plant Warehouse 8 C Tree RdMcAlester, OK 74501Required Delivery Date: Before or No Later Than September 30th, 2027.Delivery Terms: FOB Destination.1. RequirementThe Government requires the purchase and delivery of quantity 1 each, new heavy-capacity, battery-electric, counterbalanced forklift(s) for indoor industrial material-handling operations.The offered equipment shall be new, current production, and meet or exceed every minimum salient characteristic below. Used, refurbished, remanufactured, prototype, or demonstrator equipment is not acceptable.A manufacturer name, brand, or model number is not required. Offerors may propose any make or model that meets all stated requirements.2. Minimum Salient CharacteristicsCharacteristic. Minimum Requirement2.1 Equipment type. Four-wheel, sit-down, counterbalanced, battery-electric forklift suitable for heavy industrial material handling. AC Drive and Lift System.2.2 Electrical system. Battery-electric propulsion and lift system. The system shall provide performance equal to or better than a 72-volt electrical system. Shall have transistor control technology.2.3 Rated capacity. The forklift shall have a rated lifting capacity of not less than 28,700 pounds at a 24-inch load center and at a maximum fork height of 103.5 inches, with the furnished forks and fork-positioner attachment installed. Free Lift 0.0 inches with standard Load Backrest.2.4 Capacity data plate. The delivered forklift shall have a legible manufacturer capacity/data plate identifying the rated capacity for the furnished mast, forks, and attachment configuration.2.5 Mast. Two-stage mast, or functionally equivalent high visibility heavy duty mast rails configuration, capable of a maximum fork height of not less than 103.5 inches.2.6 Lowered mast height Overall lowered mast height shall not exceed 112.7 inches.2.7 Overhead guard height. Overhead guard height shall not exceed 102.56 inches.2.8 Mast tilt. Mast shall provide at least 6 degrees forward tilt and 7 degrees rearward tilt.2.9 Carriage. Pin-type carriage, or functionally equivalent carriage, compatible with the furnished fork positioner. Nominal carriage width shall be 62 inches.2.10 Forks. Furnish one pair of forks with minimum dimensions of 3.5 inches thick x 7 inches wide x 72 inches long. Forks shall be compatible with the furnished carriage and rated for the forklift/attachment configuration.2.11 Fork positioner. Furnish an integral sideshifting fork positioner Pin Type (includes 4-way Valve and 3rd and 4th Function Hosing), nominal width 62 inches, capable of both sideshift and fork-positioning functions.2.12 Hydraulic functions. Furnish all valves, controls, hydraulic lines, hoses, fittings, and other equipment required for complete operation of the fork-positioner and sideshift functions.2.13 Tires. Cushion tires, sized and load-rated by the manufacturer for the offered forklifts rated capacity and intended indoor operating surface with front tires: 28 inch x 16 inch x 22 inch (Cushion) and rear tires: 22 inch x 10 inch x 16 inch (Cushion).2.14 Steering. Full hydraulic power steering or functionally equivalent power steering with tilt steering column.2.15 Travel speed. Travel speed shall be not less than 4.8 miles per hour.2.16 Lift speed. Lift speed shall be not less than 32 feet per minute.2.17 Operator-presence protection. Furnish an operator-presence sensing system or equivalent safety interlock that prevents unintended vehicle movement or hydraulic operation when the operator is not properly positioned.2.18 Braking. Furnish a service-brake system and hand-actuated parking brake, or functionally equivalent parking-brake system.2.19 Warning devices. Furnish, at a minimum: (a) audible reverse alarm; (b) amber warning beacon/strobe; and (c) rear-facing blue warning light or equivalent visibility warning device.2.20 Rear visibility Furnish rear camera system or functionally equivalent rear-visibility aid.2.21 Lighting. Furnish forward work light(s) and rear combination light(s) suitable for normal indoor industrial operations.2.22 Operator display. Furnish an integrated operator display that includes, at a minimum, an hour meter and system-status information.2.23 Battery compartment. Forklift shall accommodate a battery compartment approximately 40 inches long x 60 inches wide, open-top configuration, or an equivalent configuration compatible with the offered forklift and required duty cycle.2.24 Battery and charger. Furnish forklift with compatible battery, charger, battery connector, and all charging accessories necessary for operation upon delivery.2.25 Warranty, complete forklift. Furnish a minimum warranty of 12 months or 2,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first, covering the complete forklift.2.26 Warranty, powertrain. Furnish a minimum powertrain warranty of 36 months or 6,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first.2.27 Manuals. Furnish one electronic and one hard-copy operators manual, maintenance manual, parts manual, and warranty documentation for each forklift.2.28 Delivery condition. Deliver forklifts fully assembled, serviced, inspected, and ready for operation.2.29 Operator orientation Provide on-site operator familiarization/orientation for Government personnel at time of delivery. Training shall address normal operation, safety features, charging requirements, daily inspection requirements, and basic preventive-maintenance actions.2.30 Compliance. The offered equipment shall comply with all applicable Federal, state, and local requirements for powered industrial trucks and workplace safety.2.31 Additional Equipment. Mechanical controls, Vinyl Semi-Susp. Seat, Operator Pres. Sens. Sys., Back-up Alarm, Rear Camera System Visibility Aid, Amber Strobe Light, Rear Facing Blue Light (Key Switch Activated), Gray SB350 Connector, Regenerative Braking, Full Hydraulic Power Steering, Hydraulic Multi-gauge, Operator Presence Sensing System (OPSS), Hand Actuated Disc Type Parking Brake, LED Headlight, Rear LED Combination Lights, Adjustable Vinyl Semi-Suspension Seat, Dual Operator Assist Grips, Hood Integrated Clipboard and Cup Holder, Durable Rubber Floor Mat, Heavy-Duty Planetary Drive Axle, Integrated Multi-Function Display w/Hour Meters, CAN-BUS interface.3. Offeror Submission RequirementsThe offeror shall submit the following with its quote or proposal:1. Manufacturer name, model number, and commercial product description.2. Manufacturer product literature, specification sheet, and dimensional drawing.3. A completed compliance matrix addressing each requirement in Section 2.4. Manufacturer documentation showing the forklifts rated capacity at the required:24-inch load center,103.5-inch maximum fork height, andfurnished fork and fork-positioner configuration.5. Description of the furnished battery, charger, connector, and charging accessories, if applicable.6. Warranty terms and authorized service-provider information.7. Proposed delivery schedule after receipt of order.Failure to provide sufficient documentation to establish compliance may render an offer ineligible for award.4. Inspection and Acceptance1. The Government will inspect the forklift(s) upon delivery.2. Acceptance is contingent upon verification that the delivered equipment:Is new and free from defects;Matches the awarded make, model, configuration, and submitted specifications.Includes all required forks, attachments, controls, safety devices, manuals, and warranty documentation.Has the required rated capacity data plate for the delivered configuration, andIs fully operational and ready for service.3. The Government may reject equipment that does not meet the salient characteristics or differs materially from the awarded offer.5. Delivery Requirements1. title: Independent Commissioning Agent (Owner�s Advocate) Services for U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT (SS) NOTIFICATION INCLUDING INDUSTRY FEEDBACK 1. Title: Independent Commissioning Agent (Owner�s Advocate) Services for U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases 2. Contracting Office: Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), R&D Contracting Division 1 - Branch 4 3. Location: Fort Detrick, Frederick, MD 4. Summary: This RFI/SS is issued solely for information and planning purposes and shall not be construed as a solicitation, restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach, or serve as an obligation on the part of the USAMRDC. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI/SS will be solely at the interested responder�s expense. Not responding to this RFI/SS does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal, if any is issued. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to Responders responding to this RFI/SS. The information resulting from this RFI/SS will determine interest and capabilities available in the marketplace; and will assist in developing acquisition strategy. 5. Background: The U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID), located at Fort Detrick, Maryland, is the premier lead medical research laboratory for the U.S. Department of War's biological defense research program. Since 1969, USAMRIID has provided leading edge medical capabilities to deter and defend against current and emerging biological threat agents. The Institute is the only laboratory in the Department of Defense equipped to safely study highly hazardous pathogens requiring maximum containment at Biosafety Level 4. USAMRIID has executed its mission from Building 1425. While historically significant, the legacy facility has surpassed its design lifespan. To sustain the DoD's biosafety integrity and research posture, the Department authorized the design and construction of a state-of-the-art replacement facility: Building 8100. Groundbreaking for the replacement complex took place in August 2009. In 2013, during the final construction execution and fit-out phases, Building 8100 experienced a fire that damaged critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure, Building Automation System controls, and associated laboratory boundary zones. Recovering from this event and achieving facility handover has become an acute operational hardship for the biodefense mission, delaying the transfer of ongoing medical research from the aging legacy facility. Note: Primary physical repair, mechanical completion, and prime construction execution are administered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE). The Contractor shall not draft new architectural designs, stamp or seal engineering drawings, or execute physical facility redesigns. 6. Scope: The Government requires an independent, third-party technical Commissioning Agent (Owner's Advocate) to bridge the technical divide between USACE/prime construction execution and the stringent operational, biosafety, and regulatory compliance requirements of the end-user (USAMRDC Headquarters and USAMRIID). The Commissioning Agent will independently evaluate, witness, and verify critical facility systems and controls, and systematically advise the Government on executing a staggered/phased transition to achieve functional occupancy, biosafety accreditation, and facility registration. How to Respond: Please submit a Capability Statement that describes relevant experience, expertise, and capabilities based upon the size and scope of this requirement as outlined in the draft Statement of Objectives (SOO). Capability statements will be reviewed/evaluated for (1) Relevant experience based on the size and scope of the outlined requirement; (2) Company specific capabilities that match the work outlined in the draft SOO. The Government will utilize the capability statements and market data collected from this notice to determine whether the proposed acquisition can be set aside for small business concerns (including 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), or HUBZone programs) or if full and open competition is required under NAICS code 541330. The formal closing date for this RFI/SS and for the submission of all responses is NLT 9 November 2026 at 12:00PM ET. All responses shall be submitted electronically using PDF or MS Word formats to the POC, Elizabeth O�Hara at elizabeth.m.ohara3.civ@health.mil. All responses received will be considered; however, a determination by the Government not to solicit the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government reserves the right to continue market research and may issue additional RFIs if deemed necessary. Each response should include the following information and must not be more than fifteen (15) pages in length: Business Information: Company name, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone, website address (if available), and the name, telephone number, and e-mail address of a point of contact having the authority and knowledge to clarify responses with Government representatives. Unique Entity ID number, CAGE Code, and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.). Companies also must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM, at www.sam.gov) to be considered as potential sources. Any and all Government Contracts/IDIQs (e.g. Federal Supply Schedule, OASIS+, etc.) you currently hold (to include the vehicle and your contract number) that could be used to fulfill this requirement. Organization Conflict of Interest: Independent verification requires that the Commissioning Agent has no conflicting roles with the facility�s prime construction contractors. Do you or any proposed team members have an active role in the construction, controls, or installation for Building 8100? Please confirm your ability to certify organizational independence in accordance with FAR RFO 9.5. Technical Experience & Biocontainment Qualifications: Interested parties are requested to provide concise, direct responses to the following four (4) topic areas. General marketing literature is discouraged. BSL-3 and BSL-4 Containment Experience: Describe your firm�s specific experience serving as an independent Commissioning Agent or Owner�s Advocate on high- and maximum containment biological facilities (BSL-3, ABSL-3, BSL-4, ABSL-4). Highlight your experience with continuous negative pressure cascades, Bubble Tight Dampers (BTDs), APR doors, chemical suit shower skids and effluent decontamination systems. Regulatory Compliance Experience: Describe your firm�s past performance conducting comprehensive gap analyses, compiling Federal Select Agent Program (FSAP) registration packages (Biosafety, Security, Incident Response, BSAT Movement Plans under 42 CFR Part 73), verifying Tier 1 physical security layouts (minimum three physical barriers), and managing a live tracking register in secure environments. title: Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management Systems Maintenance and Support Services
description: The Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), on behalf of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), is soliciting quotations for Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management System Maintenance and Support Services. This acquisition is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 561621 � Security Systems Services, with a corresponding small business size standard of $25 million in average annual receipts. Only responsible small business concerns that qualify as small under the applicable NAICS code and meet all solicitation requirements are eligible for award. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, management, materials, equipment, software licenses, technical support, and incidental services necessary to maintain FinCEN�s physical security and key-control systems. Services will be performed on an as-needed basis and may include preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, replacement, installation, relocation, testing, configuration, software support, and emergency services. The systems and equipment covered by this requirement include TRAKA electronic key-management cabinets and associated software, Medeco high-security lock cores and related hardware, Kaba Mas X10 high-security locks, other high-security and manual door-locking hardware, and associated components, cabling, licenses, and ancillary equipment. The Government anticipates awarding a time-and-materials contract with an anticipated period of performance of five years, base period and four (4) option periods. The not-to-exceed (NTE) ceiling is $40,000 for each one-year contract period. If all four option periods are exercised, the maximum potential contract ceiling is $200,000. The Contractor must be a TRAKA-authorized reseller and installer and must possess an active, final Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) at the time of award. Offerors shall provide documentation demonstrating current TRAKA authorization and the capability to maintain, repair, install, and support FinCEN�s existing TRAKA, Medeco, Kaba Mas, Lockmasters, and associated locking systems, including applicable proprietary equipment, software, licensing, integration, and compatibility requirements. Contractor personnel performing services under the resulting contract must possess final Secret personnel security clearances before beginning performance and satisfy all applicable personnel-security, continuous vetting, and facility-access requirements identified in Section 7.0 of the Statement of Work. Interim facility and personnel security clearances will not be accepted. The Government will verify the required facility clearance prior to award and personnel clearance and access requirements prior to performance. Performance will occur at FinCEN facilities located in Washington, DC, and Vienna, Virginia.

title: Europe South District Playground Inspection, Maintenance, and Repair
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is one of only two federally operated school systems in the United States. DoWEA plans, directs, coordinates, and manages pre-kindergarten through grade 12 educational programs on behalf of the Department of War (DoW). DoWEA operates approximately 165 brick-and-mortar schools across eight districts located in seven U.S. states, eleven foreign countries, Guam, and Puerto Rico, serving more than 72,000 students worldwide. DoWEA Europe consists of multiple districts encompassing schools, District Superintendent Offices (DSOs), and Student Transportation Offices (STOs) supporting children of active-duty military members and eligible civilian employees. The Contractor shall provide full-service, performance-based playground inspection, preventive maintenance, repair, emergency response, cleaning services for DoWEA facilities located in Europe South Region. For the purposes of this PWS, playgrounds include all playground systems and associated features, whether standalone or co-located, including but not limited to: Playground equipment and structures; Playground surfacing systems; Hard-surface and multi-use play courts; Outdoor recreational and athletic surfaces; and, Perimeter features, furnishings, and appurtenances. The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, tools, equipment, materials, transportation, documentation, and incidentals necessary to ensure playgrounds remain safe, serviceable, compliant, and operational throughout the period of performance.

This notice is issued solely for market research purposes and to provide industry with advance notice of a potential upcoming solicitation. A solicitation has not been issued at this time. Description: Requesting a rough order of magnitude (ROM) for estimated pricing, and capability plan, to support the purchasing and transport of materials / supplies at Veracruz, Panama to construct a 11M x 15M x 5.5M pre-engineered building with roof panels. Need the interior of the canopy to be clear space so the kids can play soccer / basketball. If you can support this request, please submit the deliverables mentioned above by 09 Novembet 2026 by 12:00PM CST. Please email information to MAJ Vernon Shank at vernon.d.shank.mil@army.mil. Thank you for the support.

title: Sources Sought - WRSU - Transportation of Human Remains
description: Purpose The Indian Health Service (IHS), White River Service Unit, is conducting market research to identify Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) capable of providing transportation services for human remains. This notice is for information and planning purposes only. It is not a solicitation or request for quotations or proposals. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or award a contract and will not reimburse costs incurred in responding. Description of Requirement The contractor shall provide transportation of human remains for purposes of autopsy as requested by White River Service Unit physicians, subject to applicable authorization and release requirements. Services include: Accepting dispatch requests from authorized White River Service Unit House Supervisors or Social Services workers. Picking up human remains within five hours of notification and transporting them from the location of death directly to the designated medical examiner�s office for autopsy. Transporting the remains, following completion of the autopsy and authorized release, to the funeral home or mortuary selected by the deceased�s family within 24 hours of autopsy completion. Performing post-autopsy repair work as needed. Drivers must hold valid driver�s licenses authorizing them to drive in Arizona and must be legally employed by an entity authorized to transport human remains within Arizona. A licensed, certified mortician is preferred. The Service Unit reported 42 autopsies requiring transportation in 2026. This historical workload is provided for planning purposes only and does not guarantee future volume. Requested Information Interested ISBEE vendors must submit both: 1. A completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form. 2. A capability statement containing: - Business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. - Unique Entity ID (UEI) and SAM.gov registration status. - A statement identifying the business as an Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE). - Relevant experience providing transportation of human remains. - Applicable business and personnel licenses or authorizations. - Ability to meet the five-hour pickup and 24-hour return requirements. - Geographic coverage, dispatch availability, personnel, vehicles, equipment, and capability to perform post-autopsy repair work. - Any anticipated subcontracting arrangements or limitations affecting performance. Responses will assist IHS in assessing the availability and capabilities of ISBEE sources and determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. Pricing is not requested at this time. Clearly identify any proprietary information included in the response.

The VA Loma Linda Healthcare System (VALLHCS), located at 11201 Benton Street, Loma Linda, CA 92357-1000 is seeking for a professional contractor to perform the annual medical gas distribution system inspection and testing. All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: Supplies/Services Refer to Price/Cost Schedule (Attached) STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) TITLE: VA Loma Linda Healthcare System s (VALLHCS) Annual Med Gas Inspection BACKGROUND INFORMATION: VA Loma Linda Healthcare System s (VALLHCS) requires a new inspection contract for Medical Gas Distribution System. The Medical gas distribution system must undergo routine source and pipeline system inspections and maintenance to ensure continuous patient safety. OBJECTIVES: VA Loma Linda Healthcare System s (VALLHCS) Medical gas distribution system inspections shall comply with NFPA99 (Health Care Facilities Code), OSHA Life safety fire code, and the ASSE 6000 standard. They require annual central supply checks, routine alarm tests, and specialized third-party inspections by certified ASSE 6020 Inspectors. The services performed shall conform to industry standards and this statement of work (SOW) and lockout and tagout procedures are to be done according to (OSHA Standard29 CFR 1910.147) VA Loma Linda Healthcare systems Policies and Regulations. SCOPE: Contractors shall provide all labor, personnel, supplies, equipment, tools, materials, supervision and other necessary items. Inspection, testing and verification are mandatory for medical gas work and will be performed by licensed ASSE 6020 Medical Gas Inspectors and ASSE 6030 Medical Gas Verifiers. Contractor shall perform Annual Medical Gas Distribution System Inspection on all Sources, Alarms, Zone Valves, and Patient Terminal Outlets / Inlets and bulk oxygen system. Including Areas as follows: Main Hospital First Floor: CLC, CLC Palliative Care, CLC Rehab, 1SW, Mod 3, Emergency department, Second Floor: ICU: 2SW, 2SE, Third Floor: OR 1 through 8, 3F-14, 3F-16, 3D-72, Recovery Room, SICU, X-Ray, MRI, Short Stay, G.I. Labs, 3NW, 3NE, 3SW, 3SE Fourth Floor: 4NW, 4NE, 4SW, 4SE, Nuclear Med, Dialysis, Blood Laboratory, Oncology Building 31 Eye Clinic Building 32 Audiology Building 30 List of items provided for inspection: Medical Gas Sources Medical air compressors, vacuum pumps, gas manifolds, and any other device used to deliver medical gases to patients. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Leak checked and documented. 3.Recommendations to comply with NFPA 99, 2024 edition Health Care Facilities Code. Master Alarm Panels Alarm panels are located at two separate locations throughout the facility. These panels monitor conditions directly from the medical gas sources. 1.Inventoried by location 2.Tested by removing existing pressure switches and other sensing devices to test the actuation points. No interruption of service is necessary if each device is mounted on code compliant demand fittings. 3.Verify proper points are being monitored at each panel. 4.Verify each panel is in the proper location. 5.Verify proper labeling. Area Alarm Panels Alarm panels that are located throughout the facility monitor medical gas pressures for the area only. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Tested by lowering pressure in each zone for each gas and documenting the alarm point. 3.Verify proper location. 4.Verify proper labeling. Zone Valve Boxes Accessible valves typically found in a corridor covered by a plastic window used mostly for emergency purposes. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Checked for leakage from packing, flange, and gauge port using oxygen safe leak detector. 3.Verify proper labeling. 4.Verify proper locations. Medical Gas Outlets/Inlets Connection points for each gas are located mostly in-patient areas. 1.Inventoried by location in each room or area inspected left to right and then top to bottom. 2.Complete an operational pressure test on each outlet and document pass/fail. (Test Parameters per NFPA 99, 2024 edition) 3.Check function of outlet/inlet and latching mechanism. 4.Check for leakage with equipment and without equipment attached. 5.Document connection type and outlet/inlet manufacturer. Oxygen Particulate Analysis Particulates are often found in existing medical gas systems due to improper installation methods that were used in the past. 1.Samples are taken on each floor in each building. Medical Air Dewpoint Analysis Moisture is removed from medical air systems at the source. Periodic Analysis of moisture throughout the facility is important to prevent possible contamination. 1.Samples are taken on each floor in each building. 2.A sample will be taken at the medical air source to compare building samples. Emergency Oxygen Supply Connection Box This box is typically mounted on the outside of a facility to facilitate the back feeding of the oxygen system if there is an interruption in service. 1.Inventoried by location. 2.Check existing location for proper compliance. 3.Check existing piping arrangements to ensure proper order of components. 4.Check to make sure box is secured. Testing to ensure all medical gas booms, and columns are leak free Most operating rooms and procedure rooms have some sort of device to help clinical personnel use the medical gases in the middle of the room by the patient. These devices are either medical gas booms or columns. The hoses and threaded connections inside these devices need to be checked periodically to ensure that there are no leaks. 1. All hoses and secondary equipment were removed from the outlets on each boom and column. 2. A test pressure for each system was observed and documented. 3. All medical gas valves were shut over a period of 10 minutes. 4. After the test period of 10 minutes passed the pressure was observed once again. 5. Any pressure drop was recorded. 6. Recommendations will be made to find existing leaks and to make repairs. Facilities responsibility: A. The facility shall coordinate with all departments to notify of the medical gas/vacuum system inspection and or repairs to be completed. B. The facility shall supply Inspecting personnel with facility maintenance personnel to unlock secured areas that have medical gas/vacuum systems, or a master key may also be supplied to complete inspection services. REPORTS: The contractor will annotate compliance with ASSE 6000, 6020 and 6030 Medical Gas specifications and requirements by submitting a detailed PM report to the Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) along with pictures for each equipment, after PM is completed. title: Rental of load bank equipment for 249th EN BAT
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS announcement for a time sensitive action; market survey for information only, to be used for preliminary planning purposes. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this synopsis. UMSB Contracting has been tasked to solicit for and award a contract for Rental of load bank equipment in support of the 249th EN BAT. A draft Statement of Work describing the requirement required has been attached. The proposed contract will be Firm Fixed Price with a period of performance from 3 DEC 2026 to 9 DEC 2026. The purpose of this DRAFT Statement of Work is to gather industry comments, suggestions, or questions before the release of the solicitation. This notice is for market research purposes only with the intent of identifying vendors that are interested and capable of performing the requirements listed in the attached DRAFT Statement of Work. The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 532490 � Other Commercial and Industry Machinery and Equipment Rental and Leasing. The capability packages for this sources sought market survey are not expected to be proposals, but rather statements regarding the company's current and past performance in relation to the areas specified in the attached document. It is asked that interested parties respond to this sources sought synopsis by completing the attached questionnaire which includes the following information: Name of the firm point of contact, phone number, email address, CAGE code, SAM UEI number, small business status and socio-economic status as listed in the System for Award Management and the corresponding NAICS code. Company's technical capability to perform a contract of this scope to include, but not limited to: Comments on the attached draft Statement of Work. Brief summary of technical capability to deliver, install, and support the required equipment listed in the Statement of Work during the specified timeframe. Does your standard 1.25 MW load bank accept a direct 4160V Delta, 3-phase, 3-wire dead break connection, or does your configuration require a step-down transformer (4160V to 480V) and additional cabling. Can your load bank derive internal control/auxiliary power directly from the 4160V source, or do you require an onboard auxiliary diesel generator / external 120V/208V power supply? Given the required operational date of December 4, 2026, what is your standard lead time for equipment mobilization, delivery, and staging? Do you provide turnkey setup, operational oversight, and teardown via certified technicians, or do you only deliver curbside equipment? Do your delivery drivers and on-site technicians possess the required credentials to access Marine Corps Base Quantico (ID)? A rough order of magnitude estimation for the entire project. Other Considerations: If there anything else your company believes the Government should consider prior to releasing a formal solicitation? This market survey is for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP). It is not to be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Government. No award will be made as a result of this market survey. All information is to be submitted at no cost or obligation to the Government. The Government reserves the right to reject, in whole or in part, any private sector input as a result of this market survey. The Government is not obligated to notify respondents of the results of this survey. Interested companies shall respond to this Sources Sought notice no later than 9 November 2026 at 1:00 P.M. ET. Responses shall be submitted via email to both the Contract Specialist, Gregory Booker at Gregory.B.Booker@usace.army.mil and the Contracting Officer, Giorgiana Chen, at Giorgiana.Chen@usace.army.mil.

description: This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). This notice is issued for market research purposes only pursuant to FAR Part 10. This notice does not obligate the Government to issue a future solicitation, award a contract, reimburse respondents for costs incurred, or otherwise pay for information submitted in response to this notice. Responses will be used to assess market capability and acquisition strategy development. USDA is conducting market research to identify commercial, academic, nonprofit, and other qualified organizations capable of providing a fully integrated weather information capability supporting the Federal Crop Insurance Program and NRCS operational requirements. The Government seeks information regarding industry capability to provide an operational, nationwide, scientifically defensible weather information service consisting of weather observations, quality control processes, terrain-aware weather modeling, historical archives, analytical tools, geospatial products, public dissemination services, restricted operational services, scientific support, and supporting infrastructure as a single integrated capability. The Government is specifically interested in determining whether capable sources exist that can provide an operational capability meeting or exceeding the functional outcomes currently relied upon by USDA programs. The Government seeks capability statements from organizations capable of delivering a complete end-to-end weather information service that supports: Federal Crop Insurance Program operations Weather validation activities Weather-related underwriting and claims analysis Prevented planting determinations Historical weather reconstruction Program integrity reviews NRCS data estimation and quality-control operations Public dissemination of weather information Scientific analysis and support The Government is not seeking individual datasets, individual models, isolated software applications, consulting-only services, or limited analytical support. The Government seeks information regarding complete integrated capabilities. Required Capability Areas Respondents shall address their current operational capabilities within the following major areas. 1. Integrated Operational Capability The respondent shall demonstrate an existing operational capability providing: Ground-based observation acquisition Observation quality assurance/quality control Terrain-aware weather modeling Historical weather archives Weather product generation Geospatial services Public dissemination Restricted operational user services Analytical tools Scientific support Infrastructure and operations The complete capability shall be currently available. 2. Observation Acquisition and Quality Control The Government seeks information regarding: Use of federal, state, tribal, academic, cooperative, public, and commercial weather networks. Integration of NRCS station data from the Water and Climate Information System (WCIS) Air and Water Database (AWDB). Use of CoCoRaHS observations. Use of state and regional Mesonet data. Station metadata validation. Observation lineage and traceability. Automated and manual QA/QC processes. Observation anomaly detection and resolution procedures. Respondents should describe operational processes, governance, documentation, and evidence supporting these capabilities. 3. Weather Modeling The Government seeks information regarding operational terrain-aware weather modeling capable of: Incorporating elevation effects. Incorporating slope and exposure influences. Accounting for rain-shadow impacts. Addressing coastal influences. Producing scientifically supportable estimates in sparse observation environments. Integrating observations and model output into operational products. Respondents should describe model architecture, operational status, validation methods, and production workflows. 4. National Weather Products The Government seeks operational capabilities providing: Gridded precipitation. Maximum temperature. Minimum temperature. Products shall be available for: CONUS Alaska Hawaii Products should support operational delivery at nominal spatial resolutions of 800 meters or finer. 5. Historical Archive and Data Stewardship The Government seeks information regarding: Historical archives extending at least thirty years. Product version management. Historical reproducibility. Metadata preservation. Revision tracking. Product lineage documentation. 6. Derived Agricultural Weather Products The Government seeks information regarding operational generation of: Weather normals Ten-year averages Weather departures from normal Growing degree days Chilling hours Aggregated weather statistics Agricultural weather indicators Respondents should describe methodologies and reproducibility controls. 7. Crop Insurance Operational Support The Government seeks information regarding support for: Claims validation Underwriting analysis Prevented planting reviews Historical event reconstruction Authorized litigation support Program integrity reviews Convergence-of-evidence weather analysis 8. Restricted Operational Services The Government seeks information regarding secure operational portals that provide authorized users with: Weather reports Maps Historical analyses Downloadable geospatial data Raster-based analytical processing Repeatable analytical workflows Downloadable outputs Respondents should describe scalability, availability, auditability, lineage tracking, and security controls. 9. Public Dissemination The Government seeks information regarding operational public-access services that: Provide designated weather products without subscription fees. Publish historical and current weather data. Maintain public metadata and methodology documentation. Support public download of designated weather products. 10. Scientific Support The Government seeks information regarding scientific staffing and support including: PhD-level scientists with expertise in meteorology, climatology, hydrology, atmospheric science, agricultural weather, geospatial science, or related disciplines. Direct engagement with RMA subject matter experts. Direct engagement with NRCS subject matter experts. Expertise in weather observation systems, modeling, quality control, validation, statistics, geospatial analysis, and operational support. 11. NRCS-Specific Requirements The Government seeks information regarding capabilities supporting: SNOTEL SNOLITE SCAN including: Daily estimates Historical estimates API services Performance metrics Data lineage Estimation methodologies Quality-control portals Non-stationarity analyses Information Requested Interested organizations shall provide: 1. Corporate Information Company name UEI CAGE Code Business size Socioeconomic status Primary points of contact 2. Capability Statement A narrative describing the firm's capability to provide the complete integrated service. 3. Compliance Matrix Provide a requirement-by-requirement response for all mandatory requirements identified in Attachment 1. For each requirement, identify: Compliant Partially Compliant Not Compliant For each response include: Operational status Objective evidence Description of capability Dependencies Data restrictions Licensing restrictions Government-furnished requirements Transition requirements Staffing requirements Assumptions 4. Operational Readiness Identify which capabilities are: Fully operational today Operational with minor enhancements In development Planned / conceptual Respondents shall not represent conceptual or planned functionality as current operational capability. 5. Transition Approach Describe how continuity of operations would be maintained during transition while avoiding disruption to RMA and NRCS operations. 6. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Provide a non-binding ROM estim

Does your standard 1.25 MW load bank accept a direct 4160V Delta, 3-phase, 3-wire dead break connection, or does your configuration require a step-down transformer (4160V to 480V) and additional cabling? Can your load bank derive internal control/auxiliary power directly from the 4160V source, or do you require an onboard auxiliary diesel generator / external 120V/208V power supply? Do you provide turnkey setup, operational oversight, and teardown via certified technicians, or do you only deliver curbside equipment? Do your delivery drivers and on-site technicians possess the required credentials to access Marine Corps Base Quantico (ID)? A rough order of magnitude estimation for the entire project. description: SECTION A � Solicitation Executive Summary 1. The Government will procure the requirements utilizing the three-step procurement outlined below. Step One: A Pre-solicitation Notice will not be submitted separately, as this notice will be encompassed together with the Request for Quotation and released in SAM.gov. The website for SAM is https://www.sam.gov. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial supplies prepared in accordance with the format in FAR RFO 12.202, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes only the solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a formal solicitation will NOT be issued. An annual synopsis for requirements falling under the scope of this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will NOT be released in SAM.gov, despite any emergent requirements that may arise throughout the years. Attachment 0001 � Scope of Work Portfolio - Lumber BOA lists the lumber products to be ordered against this BOA, however, it is not limited to the list provided. Specific evaluation criteria for specific requirements shall be communicated with each BOA Delivery Order. The Offeror must demonstrate the capability to deliver, at a minimum, the specified lumber requirements to at least one (1) of the seven (7) military installations designated in this solicitation. Material MAY be inspected through the Government Quality Assurance (QA) Department. This will be determined at each Delivery Order level. The contractor MAY BE REQUIRED TO provide a Certificate of Conformance (COC) and Certified Test Report for all processes indicating contractor compliance with all associated tech data requirements. This will be determined at each Delivery Order level. The solicitation and incorporated provisions and clauses included in the resulting BOA master agreements are incorporated under Attachment 0002 and are in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 and made a part of each Government delivery order under the BOA. If any clauses are revised during the life of this BOA, the most recently dated version of the clause shall apply. The NAICS code for this procurement is 321113 (Sawmills). The small business standard for this NAICS is 550 employees. The Product Service Code is 5510 (Lumber). Step Two: The Basic Ordering Agreement Request for Quotation (BOA RFQ) will be released one time to allow interested contractors an opportunity to submit a quotation for evaluation to obtain an executed McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (MCAAP) BOA. The Government will execute no-cost BOAs to offerors whose quotations in response to those solicitations are found acceptable on the criteria stated in the RFQ. The BOAs will be valid for a period of up to five (5) years beginning from the effective date of the initial BOA execution. NOTE: This BOA RFQ will be the only opportunity contractors have to obtain an executed Lumber BOA award to propose on Delivery Order RFQs issued within the next five (5) years. BOA quotations will not be solicited, accepted, and will not be executed at any other time, even for those emergent requirements not specifically identified in the initial synopsis. Therefore, if a contractor desires to participate in ANY future Lumber delivery order that may arise within the next five (5) years, it is imperative that the contractor submit a quotation in response to this Rigging BOA RFQ. Step Three: The Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) will issue competitive Delivery Order RFQs for specific requirements falling under the scope of the Lumber BOA. An offeror must be a qualified BOA holder as of the closing date of a delivery order solicitation. The Government will confirm that an offeror is a qualified BOA holder by checking the effective date of an offeror�s BOA. Delivery Order RFQs will result in a Requirement contract. Section C of this RFQ includes exceptions for requirements performed by Ability One or 8(a) contractors. 2. The following are the current known requirements: Lumber provided under multiple Basic Ordering Agreements (BOA) to the following seven (7), but not limited installations: Anniston Army Depot Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) Letterkenny Munitions Command (LEMC) McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (MCAAP) Tooele Army Depot (TEAD) Joint Munitions Technology Center (JMTC) DELIVERY SCHEDULE The offeror must demonstrate capability to deliver ordered materials to the designated installation delivery point within 14 business days after receipt of standard Delivery Orders and seven (7) business days after receipt of emergency Delivery Orders. On time delivery is very critical; therefore, the offeror must adhere to the delivery requirements indicated in each Delivery Order. Failure to comply with the contractual delivery schedule after award may result in termination of the order or required to extend a delivery schedule if offerors encounter delays. The non-availability of raw materials, sub quoter issues, scheduling conflicts, etc. are not acceptable excuses for failing to meet the delivery schedules. Early delivery may be authorized but must be approved and coordinated in advance of due date with the contract specialist and contracting officer designated in each Delivery Order. If there is going to be a delay in delivery, the offeror is required to notify the contract specialist and contracting officer designated in the Delivery Order within 24 hours of knowledge of that delay. title: PLA RFI for Repair of Waterfront Utility Services Transmitted via a Utilidor Tunnel at NSB Kings Bay, GA
description: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) Request for Information (RFI) for Construction Project for building in the State of Georgia Repair Waterfront Utility Services at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, GA. This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) SE is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project is for the repair of waterfront utility services transmitted via a Utilidor tunnel to Refit Wharves and the Drydock using a phased approach in order to not impact ongoing operations. The project will repair potable water, fire protection, and process water piping; and replace associated hangers and supports and valves. Additionally, it will repair chilled water piping and insulation jackets, and repairs to sanitary sewer piping, oily waste piping, industrial wastewater/saltwater piping, and repair concrete access covers to the Utilidor tunnel. The project located in the State of Georgia. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 237110. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $100,000,000 - $150,000,000. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 630 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.502-2(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. This is not an announcement of the availability of a solicitation nor is it a means of generating a plan holder�s list. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to John Mack john.e.mack5.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00 pm Eastern Time on November 09, 2026.

Background: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Division of Police, is responsible for providing and administering contract guard services at specific buildings and entrances both on and off the NIH campus in the Washington-Baltimore area to supplement security systems and law enforcement personnel. To provide independent quality validation of this contract guard force, free of the bias inherent in self-assessment, NIH separately acquires performance management and surveillance services of the guard force vendor from a different contractor not involved in day-to-day security operations. This surveillance function is critical to validating that contract security guard services are performed at a continuous, acceptable quality level, helping prevent weaponized vehicles and unauthorized personnel from entering the NIH main campus and satellite facilities. There are currently 22 separate posts/locations on the main campus and 9 off-campus sites with contract guards assigned, several staffed 24 hours a day, located throughout the greater Washington-Baltimore region including Bethesda, Baltimore, Fort Detrick, Poolesville, and Rockville, Maryland. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of this acquisition is to procure surveillance and quality assurance services of NIH's contract security guard force, consistent with the Guard Force Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan / Performance Requirements Summary (QASP/PRS). Project requirements: Independently, and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall perform the following: Conduct random, scheduled, and unscheduled inspections/surveillance of the contract guard force at all NIH facilities in the Washington-Baltimore area with assigned contract guards, during all hours of the day and night, including holidays, weekends, and periods of inclement weather. Evaluate guard force performance across five categories: Access Control; Roving Patrols; Training and Recruitment; Professional Guard Service and Complaint Monitoring; and Continuous Improvement/Contract Reporting. Conduct surreptitious attempts to penetrate perimeter vehicle entrances and building entrances, including testing vehicle entry points from a vehicle operator's position, using contractor-provided and maintained vehicles. Report negative surveillance findings to the NIH Contracting Officer's Representative and Division of Police within 30 minutes of an observed infraction, with electronic data entry follow-up. Provide immediate/next-business-day written reports for reportable incidents (e.g., vacant posts, validated sleeping-on-post infractions, incidents involving designated NIH senior officials), plus weekly, monthly, and quarterly summary reporting. Provide personnel deployment schedules not less than two weeks in advance. Maintain staffing capable of maintaining telephone communication with NIH at all times while performing assigned duties. Document surveillance processes for each facility/location within 90 to 120 days of surveillance beginning at that location. All assigned personnel must maintain required security clearances, undergo background investigation, and comply with HSPD-12 requirements for access to NIH secure areas. Locality Requirement: Per the Statement of Objectives for this requirement, the contractor shall maintain an administrative office within 100 miles of the NIH campus, to facilitate regular coordination between the Project Officer and the Contractor. Anticipated period of performance: Base Year: March 21, 2027 � March 20, 2028 Option Year 1: March 21, 2028 � March 20, 2029 Option Year 2: March 21, 2029 � March 20, 2030 Option Year 3: March 21, 2030 � March 20, 2031 Option Year 4: March 21, 2031 � March 20, 2032 6-Month Option To Extend: March 21, 2032 � September 20, 2032 Requested Response: The intent of this sources sought notice is to help define the procurement strategy (e.g., set-aside, sole source, unrestricted) for a solicitation intended to be posted at a later date. Interested contractors are requested to respond by (1) describing their relevant experience and capability to perform surveillance/quality assurance services of the kind described above, including not less than five years of experience in Quality Assurance Inspections/Surveillance related to the security field and performance-based contracts; and (2) providing a capability statement demonstrating their bona fide ability to perform this requirement within the time frame described above. In addition, please state your business size status and whether you maintain, or would be able to establish, an administrative office within 100 miles of the NIH campus. Please note that NIH is particularly interested in small business sources. If you are a small business, please state the type of small business (small business; HUBZone; service-disabled, veteran-owned; 8(a); veteran-owned; woman-owned; or small disadvantaged businesses) and your size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. The Ombudsman Program for Agency Protests (OPAP) was established to address protest issues within the agency, providing an alternative to costly and time-consuming litigation. Operating independently, OPAP offers relief comparable to that granted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO). Interested parties are encouraged to resolve concerns through USDA�s internal Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) process before pursuing external forums such as the GAO. Concerns may be addressed informally or through a formal agency protest filed with either the Contracting Officer or the Ombudsman. Informal Forum with the Ombudsman 1. Initial Point of Contact: Interested parties who believe a specific USDA procurement is unfair or otherwise defective should first direct their concerns to the applicable Contracting Officer. 2. Escalation: If the Contracting Officer is unable to address their concerns, interested parties are encouraged to contact the USDA Ombudsman for Agency Protests. Under this informal process, the agency is not required to suspend contract award performance. Utilization of the informal forum does not suspend any time requirement for filing a formal protest with the agency or other forums. 3. Required Information: To ensure a timely response, interested parties should provide the following information to the Ombudsman: solicitation/contract number, contracting office, Contracting Officer, and solicitation closing date (if applicable). Effort to Resolve: Prior to submitting a formal agency protest, protesters must first use their best efforts to resolve their concerns with the Contracting Officer through open and frank discussions. 2. Independent Review: If the protester�s concerns remain unresolved, an Independent Review is available by the Ombudsman. The protester may file a formal agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or, alternatively, with the Ombudsman under the OPAP program. Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined in writing to be in the best interest of the Government. 3. Resolution Timeline: The agency�s goal is to resolve protests within 35 calendar days from the date of filing. 4. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104(a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. 5. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. 6. Submission: Formal protests under the OPAP program should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Election of Forum. The US Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistic Center, Alameda CA is seeking contractors interested in providing Maintenance and Repair Services with DRYDOCK AVAILABILITY FY2027 for the USCGC ASPEN (WLB-208) FY27 Drydock Availability. The US Coast Guard Cutter ASPEN (WLB-208) is a 225' seagoing buoy tender homeported at: 4688 Homer Spit Road. Home, AK 99603. Work list will include but is not limited to: Drydocking of a vessel 225ft in length, inspection/maintenance/ and preservation of underwater body paint/hull/ and buoy deck anchor chain, maintenance to rudder/propeller/thrusters/ and shafting, cleaning of ballast/sewage/fuel tanks and piping, crane/deck equipment work, and renewal of sea valves and strainers There are approximately 108 Line Items. ***PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT*** 1. A WLB's design limits its use to protected and inland waters. The cutter is not crewed for continuous steaming and is normally limited to daylight transits. Due to crewing and cutter employment standards, seven days transit is the limit of crew endurance under normal operating conditions. Ten hours of transit per day is the planning factor due to crew fatigue. WLB's have a maximum speed of 10 knots, however, environmental factors frequently limit average speed to 6.5 knots. 2. title: USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) Request for Proposal(s)
description: The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) issues solicitation N00024-26-R-4421 for the execution of the USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA). This Signature Availability includes a combination of maintenance, modernization, and repair, and will require highly capable contractors with substantial facilities, to include capable pier (for the applicable ship class) as well as human resources capable of completing, coordinating, and integrating multiple areas of ship maintenance, repair and modernization. This Signature Availability is solicited on a coast-wide basis on the West Coast under a single solicitation, and one (1) contract to complete the availability is expected to be awarded to one (1) contractor. Based on the complexity, magnitude and duration of the requirement, the Governments market research indicates there are not two or more small business concerns capable of competing for these requirements and therefore this procurement will not be set aside for small business (FAR 19.502-2(b)). This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested parties must comply with this announcement. Interested offerors should monitor the PlEE.gov and SAM.gov pages for the release of the solicitation and any applicable amendments, thereafter. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to participate in this procurement at https://www.sam.gov. All responsible sources may submit a proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to all applicable CDRLs, J- and S- attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Jacob Juros at jacob.a.juros.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Brian Romano, at brian.c.romano.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your companys SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. ***NOTICE*** In addition, there are references that contain limiting distribution statements and will not be disseminated from the Contract Specialist. In these instances, Offerors shall contact the Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) Technical Librarian at swrmc.techdocs@us.navy.mil to arrange access per RFP Section L instruction. Offerors shall review Section L, General Information for further details. ***END NOTICE***The Government anticipates making a single award in or before March 2027. USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 DSRA will begin in November 2027 with an expected completion in October 2029.

title: F--Post-Flood Cleanup and Disaster AbatementSand Is
description: Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (Commercial Item) FAR References: FAR Part 12; FAR 5.203; FAR 19.502-2 (Total Small Business Set-Aside) NAICS Code: 562910 - Remediation Services Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Product Service Code: F108 - Environmental Systems Protection - Environmental Remediation Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Unit Price Description of Requirement The Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Canyon Country District, has an immediate abatement need for post-flood cleanup and disaster abatement at the Sand Island Ranger Station, located in a remote area approximately 4 miles west of Bluff, Utah. Flooding resulted from the San Juan River overtopping its banks and affected the following structures: * Boat House (~1,800 SF open warehouse) * Visitor Contact Center (~700 SF office/exhibition space - straw bale construction) * Law Enforcement Office (~400 SF office and sleeping area) * Residential Unit (~1,800 SF manufactured home - work primarily limited to the crawl space) The work includes hazard assessment, moisture mapping and documentation, standing water removal and drying, muck removal (excluding the residential unit), removal of saturated flooring and baseboards, replacement of drywall where appropriate, HEPA air scrubbing, and proper disposal of debris. A detailed Statement of Work is attached. Only vendors capable of mobilizing quickly to a remote location in southeastern Utah and performing the required abatement work should compete for award. This is an urgent requirement. Work is expected to begin as soon as possible following award. Period of performance is 30 calendar days from Notice to Proceed. The Notice to Proceed will be issued no later than three (3) calendar days after award. Site Visit A site visit is scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Mountain Time. Interested firms are strongly encouraged to attend. Meeting Location: Sand Island Ranger Station parking area (upper lot). The Government representative will be available in the parking area. Health Advisory: The San Juan County Health Department detected E. coli in the flood waters at 25 times the typical level. Vendors should take all appropriate precautions. Vendors attending the site visit must bring all necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate for flood-damaged structures and potentially contaminated environments. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest.
