Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. title: USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) Request for Proposal(s)
description: The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) issues solicitation amendment N00024-26-R-4421 A0001 for the execution of the USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA). This Signature Availability includes a combination of maintenance, modernization, and repair, and will require highly capable contractors with substantial facilities, to include capable pier (for the applicable ship class) as well as human resources capable of completing, coordinating, and integrating multiple areas of ship maintenance, repair and modernization. description: This is a Notice of Intent to issue a sole source contract and is not a request for competitive quotes/proposals. Description of effort: Provide advisory and assistance services (A&AS) to the DoW Cooperative Threat Reduction (CTR) Program in managing and executing programs across the Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) spectrum as part of the broader countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD) mission. The A&AS provides the necessary expertise in achieving key U.S. national security objectives, as outlined in the National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and the DoD CWMD Strategy through subject matter experts (SMEs) in the applicable technical, international agreements, foreign partner country regulatory, foreign partner program sustainment, integrated product team and working group, acquisition, logistics management, financial, strategic planning, training, information technology, security, and administrative support. This contract is intended to ensure the uninterrupted continuation of the DoW CTR Program�s critical mission through the award of a bridge contract to continue external professional A&AS specialized support and technical expertise.

title: Repair of Waterfront Utility Services Transmitted via a Utilidor Tunnel at NSB Kings Bay, GA
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS FOR A DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT TO REPAIR WATERFRONT UTILITY SERVICES TRNASMITTED VIA A UTILIDOR TUNNEL AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE KINGS BAY, GA. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RM610. The purpose of this notice is for the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) to gain knowledge of ALL qualified and interested parties. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), and service disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB). Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform this proposed project. The Government may use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement. Project Description: Project will repair waterfront utility services -- originating in Building 5091 --transmitted via the Utilidor tunnel -- to all three Trident Refit Facilities (TRF) Refit Wharves and the Drydock utilizing a phased approach in order not to impact ongoing operations. The project will repair potable water, fire protection, and process water piping; and replace associated hangers and supports and valves. Additionally, it will repair chilled water piping and insulation jackets, and repairs to sanitary sewer piping, oily waste piping, industrial wastewater/saltwater piping, and repair concrete access covers to the Utilidor tunnel at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, Ga. Construction shall meet or exceed requirements of the 2024 International Building Code (IBC), NFPA 101, and Unified Facility Criteria (UFC). The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 630 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $100,000,000 and $150,000,000. The anticipated award date is fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this Sources Sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-7). Complete submission package shall not exceed 6 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) if applicable for NAICS Code 237110 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $150 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS Number). 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6) Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of four (4) projects demonstrating the specific capabilities listed below: Complex Industrial Utility Systems (e.g. Potable Water, Chilled water sewer, industrial waste) Major Electrical System Upgrades (e.g. 5kV-35KV electrical distribution systems, transformers, switch gears Installation of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at $40 million or greater and completed within the past seven (7) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including contract number, project title, completion date, performance ratings, and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. Please respond to this announcement no later than 09 NOV 2026, 2:00 PM Eastern Time via email to aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil and john.e.mack5.civ@us.navy.mil. The subject line of the email shall state: NSB Kings Bay, Utilidor. Emails shall be no more than 5 MB in size. Responses that do not meet all requirements or are not submitted within the allotted time will not be considered. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

description: This project consists of providing all materials, equipment, labor, transportation, and incidentals for completion of the repair storm damage sustained on three buildings at this site. The repairs are to include roof replacement, dry wall and insulation replacement, a door replacement, ceiling and insulation replacement, installation of gutters and downspouts, and to replace a portion of the side of the Chino Yard Office; to perform maintenance to the metal roofs on the Supervisor�s office and the Chino Shop; to repair window frames on upper windows, to caulk ALL of windows, and to install a Z bar at the roof line on the Supervisor�s Office; and to gutters and downspouts on the Chino Shop. This project could also include, if additional funds are available, optional bid items. The optional bid items are exterior painting on the Yard Office; replace the weather stripping on two garage doors and a door sweep on a manway; and if mold is found in the Supervisor�s Office to replace the dry wall and insulation.

description: The Government intends to procure, under only one responsible source, where no other suppliers or service will satisfy the agency requirements. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Hawaii (NAVFAC Hawaii) is conducting market research to determine if other potential products/services can provide for an electrical meter that has equal performance requirements as the Schneider Electric PowerLogic ION8650 Power and Energy, manufactured by Schneider Electric USA, Inc., 800 Federal St, Andover, MA 01810-1067. The alternate product/service must meet the following requirements/specifications: Listed on AF�s Advanced Meter Reading System (AMRS) Compliant Meter List Meter must comply with ANSI C12.1, NEMA C12.19, and ANSI C12.20 and must match existing AMRS reading system at the installation. Meter must be rated for use at temperature from minus 40 degrees Centigrade to plus 70 degrees Centigrade. The meters must have an electronic demand recording register and must be secondary reading as indicated. The register must be used to indicate maximum kilowatt demand as well as cumulative or continuously cumulative demand. Demand must be measured on a block-interval basis and must be capable of a 5 to 60 minute interval and initially set to a 15-minute interval. It must have provisions to be programmed to calculate demand on a rolling interval basis. Meter readings must be true RMS. The meter electronic register must be of modular design with non-volatile data storage. Downloading meter stored data must be capable via an optical port. Recording capability of data storage with a minimum capability of 89 days of 15 minute, 2 channel interval data. The meter must be capable of providing at least 2 KYZ pulse outputs (dry contacts). Meter must have an optical port on front of meter. Optical device must be compatible with ANSI C12.18. Meters must be 120-480 volts auto ranging. Power Quality: sag/swell, individual, even, odd, total harmonics to the 31st and symmetrical components 9S, 35S, 36S socket and switchboard cases True RMS 3-phase voltage, current, power and meets ANSI revenue metering standards including ANSI C12.20 0.2 and Class 2, 10, & 20. This notification is for market research purposes only and should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the U.S. Government to issue a solicitation, request for proposals, quotes, or invitation of bids or award a contract. Interested parties with a comparable product meeting the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit complete technical data, information and specifications in order for the Government to conduct an evaluation of your product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. Technical response shall be typed, at least 11 point Times New Roman or larger, single-sided 8.5 by 11 inch pages and submitted in Adobe PDF format. Also, provide company information and point of contract (name, title, email, phone, mailing address). The Government will not reimburse any responder for any costs associated with information submitted in response to this sources sought announcement. Any information provided to the Government in response to this request for information (RFI) will become U.S. Government property and will not be returned. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit your company brochure. Interested parties shall submit information and specifications to Shae Ishimoto, Contract Specialist, via email at shae.n.ishimoto.civ@us.navy.mil. Interested parties responding to this announcement by 9 November, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. Hawaii Standard Time will be considered.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE W912DW27X1CUL Bulk Propane Delivery Services � Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam, Washington NAICS Code: 325120 � Industrial Gas Manufacturing THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This notice is not a solicitation, request for quotation, request for proposal, or commitment by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) to issue a solicitation, award a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in responding. 1. Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Seattle District, is conducting market research to identify responsible and capable sources that can provide bulk propane delivery services to the following Government facilities in Washington State: Howard Hanson Dam, 36932 SE Green River Headworks Road, Ravensdale, WA 98051 Mud Mountain Dam, 30525 SE Mud Mountain Road, Enumclaw, WA 98022-8010 USACE anticipates establishing one or more commercial Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) to support recurring propane requirements. The Government anticipates placing BPA calls as needed for tank refills during the BPA ordering period. The Government is using NAICS 325120, Industrial Gas Manufacturing, for purposes of this market research. Interested parties should identify the NAICS code(s) and size standard under which they consider themselves eligible for this requirement. 2. Anticipated Requirement The anticipated requirement is for the delivery of commercial bulk propane to Government-owned or Government-designated propane tanks at Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam. The anticipated services may include: - Routine bulk propane deliveries as requested by the Government; - Emergency and/or after-hours propane deliveries; - Delivery to multiple sites under individual BPA calls; - Delivery-ticket documentation showing, at a minimum, date and time of delivery, delivery location, quantity delivered in gallons, unit price, applicable fees, and total price; - Compliance with applicable safety, transportation, environmental, and site-access requirements; - Coordination with designated Government points of contact; - Optional tank-level monitoring or vendor-managed delivery services, if commercially available and proposed. The Government anticipates that refill quantities, timing, and annual consumption may vary based on weather, operational requirements, and tank capacity. The Government does not guarantee any minimum quantity of propane or minimum number of calls. Estimated annual gallons, anticipated tank sizes, historical usage data, delivery access information, and anticipated BPA ordering period may be provided in any future solicitation, if issued. 3. Market Research Information Requested Interested parties are requested to provide a capability statement addressing the following: A. Company Information 1. Company name, physical address, website, and primary point of contact. 2. Point-of-contact name, title, telephone number, and email address. 3. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 4. CAGE code, if applicable. 5. Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 325120, including, as applicable: - Small business; - Small disadvantaged business; - Woman-owned small business; - HUBZone small business; - Service-disabled veteran-owned small business; and/or - Veteran-owned small business. 6. Identify any applicable GSA Schedule, Governmentwide Acquisition Contract, existing BPA, or other Federal contract vehicle through which the company currently provides propane or related fuel-delivery services. B. Capability and Service Coverage 1. Describe the company�s experience providing bulk propane delivery services to commercial, municipal, Federal, industrial, remote, or critical-infrastructure customers. 2. State whether the company can provide service to: - Howard Hanson Dam; and - Mud Mountain Dam. 3. Identify the normal service area, dispatch location(s), and approximate distance or travel time to each dam location. 4. Identify whether the company can provide tank-level monitoring, automatic refill, telemetry, or other inventory-management support. Describe any associated equipment, fees, data access, maintenance responsibilities, and cybersecurity or connectivity considerations. C. Commercial Pricing Practices The Government is particularly interested in understanding commercial pricing practices for propane deliveries in western Washington. Please address the following: 1. Describe how the company establishes its bulk propane prices for commercial or government customers. 2. Identify whether the company uses a published propane-price index, rack price, wholesale market index, or other objective benchmark. 3. If an index is used, identify: - The name of the index or publication; - The geographic market point or terminal; - The frequency of publication; - The date used to determine the price�for example, date of order, date before delivery, date of delivery, or another defined date; and - Whether the index value is available to the Government for invoice verification. 4. Identify any non-commodity charges that may apply, including: - Delivery fees; - Site-specific delivery fees; - Fuel or transportation surcharges; - Hazmat, environmental, or administrative fees; - Minimum-delivery charges; - Emergency or after-hours fees; - Tank rental, lease, maintenance, or monitoring fees; - Taxes; and - Any other recurring or one-time charges. 5. Describe whether these charges can be proposed as fixed rates for the BPA ordering period. E. Contracting and BPA Input 1. Identify any recommended BPA terms, ordering procedures, delivery requirements, pricing methods, or commercial practices the Government should consider. F. Response Instructions Interested parties shall submit a capability statement of no more than five (5) pages, excluding attachments, in PDF format. Responses shall be emailed to: Contract Specialist: Monique Paano Email: Monique.a.paano@usace.army.mil Subject Line: �Sources Sought Response � Bulk Propane Delivery � Howard Hanson Dam and Mud Mountain Dam� Responses are due no later than November 9, 2026 at noon Pacific Time. Cage _______ ref. no. ;34228 100148; 3.2 Marking - This item shall be physically identified in accordance with ;MIL-STD-130, REV N, 16 NOV 2012; . 3.3 Changes in Design, Material Servicing, or Part Number - Except for a Code 1 change, which shall be processed as provided in the code statement shown below, no substitution of items shall be made until the NAVICP-MECH Contracting Officer has notified and approval has been given by issuance of a written change order. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation or via amendment. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend.

Requirements Overview 5.1 Basic Services: Sewage pumping and drain clearing is directly related to public health and sanitation and is essential to CVD/ Lake Mendocino�s recreation mission. The Contractor shall furnish all equipment, supplies, items, labor, materials, and services necessary to for sewage pumping and proper disposal, drain clearing, portable toilet rental, and portable/vault toilet stall cleaning/treatment in accordance with all federal, state, and local regulations. 5.2 Service Descriptions: 5.2.1 Lift Stations & Holding Tanks: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each tank (including all litter and refuse such as bottles, trash bags, clothing, etc.), and hose down the area around the tank ensuring any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. The removed waste shall be transported from CVD/ Lake Mendocino and disposed of in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Contractor shall bear all cost in connection with this work. Tank capacities throughout the park vary from 1,000 � 10,000 gallons. Tank locations are outlined in Attachment 1 Work Site Area & Sewage Locations. 5.2.2 Vault Toilets: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each tank/vault. This includes all litter and refuse (bottles, cans, trash bags, clothing, etc.), which can be a common occurrence in the public vault toilets at Lake Mendocino. The Contractor shall also recharge the tank/vault with approximately one foot of water after pumping, apply an enzyme treatment if needed, and hose down the area around the tank ensuring any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. An enzyme treatment may be needed to control odor and maintain cleanliness of the stall. The removed waste shall be transported from CVD/ Lake Mendocino and disposed of in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Contractor shall bear all cost in connection with this work. Vault toilets have a capacity of 1,000 gallons per stall. Vault toilet locations are outlined in Attachment 1. 5.2.3 Sewer and Drain Line Clearing: The Contractor shall provide any combination of video camera services, snaking, rooting, hydro-jetting, and/or chemical treatment necessary to identify and remedy drain line clogs such that the lines can flow freely. Lines that do not continue to flow freely for one week (7 days) will require re-work at no additional cost to the Government. 5.2.4 Portable Toilets: 5.2.4.1 Amount, Type, and Condition: Locations subject to portable toilet placement include recreation areas outlined in Attachment 1. This will primarily be in areas with flush restrooms that occasionally experience system failures. The Contractor shall have enough inventory 15 available to be able to provide up to four (4) sets of portable toilets at one time. A set includes one regular size portable toilet and one ADA-compliant size portable toilet. Portable toilets shall be for outdoor-use and anchorable. The Contractor shall maintain portables that are clean and in good repair, free of significant odors, damage, and vandalism. Stalls must have adequate ventilation, be uniformly painted, constructed such that walls provide adequate privacy, and have doors with a working lock mechanism. Portables should be delivered and placed on flat, level ground surfaces as directed by the COR. In the event portables are vandalized, damaged, and/or moved by the public, the Contractor bears the responsibility of retrieving, repairing and/or replacing them. At the discretion of the COR, the Contractor shall remove and replace damaged portables with ones in good condition. There are also two (2) USACE-owned portable toilets that are subject to service. The Contractor is not responsible for the good working condition of these portables but is required to follow the same service description outlined below in Section 5.2.4.3 for the same unit price as the Contractor-owned portables. 5.2.4.2 Rental Period: The Contractor shall deliver portable toilets in good working conditions within 48 hours of request by the COR. Portable toilets will be rented per type per two-week (15-day) period. 5.2.4.3 Service: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each portable, transport the waste from CVD/ Lake Mendocino, and dispose of it in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Additionally, each portable should be recharged with an industry standard deodorant/cleaner, restocked with reasonably enough toilet paper to last until the next service, and thoroughly cleaned. Cleaning includes scrubbing, wiping, rinsing, removing with appropriate soaps, disinfectants, and cleaning solutions to ensure stall floors, walls, ceilings, door, toilet lids, and toilet risers are free from waste, refuse, residues, spider webs, and significant odors. The area should be hosed down around the portables if needed to ensure any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. 5.3 Frequency: The Contractor shall provide services on a call-out basis. Scheduling for services will be agreed upon between the Contractor and the COR prior to the delivery of services. The allotted quantities for each service per this contract are based on field experiences from the past five (5) years and best estimates for future needs. description: DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS REGIONAL PROCUREMENT OFFICE (RPO) WEST NETWORK CONTRACTING OFFICE 17 (NCO 17) 5441 Babcock Road, Suite 302, San Antonio, TX 78240 SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Energy Center Steam Header and Boiler Valve, Gasket, and Vent Line Replacement VA North Texas Health Care System Dallas VA Medical Center, Dallas, Texas NOTICE INFORMATION Notice ID 36C25727Q0078 Notice Type Sources Sought (Market Research) Posted Date October 30, 2026 Response Deadline November 9, 2026, 2:00 p.m. Central Time Contracting Office Department of Veterans Affairs, RPO West | NCO 17 | Lab Services Support (LSS), 5441 Babcock Road, Suite 302, San Antonio, TX 78240 Primary Point of Contact Ognian D. Lancaster Road, Dallas, TX 75216 1. PURPOSE This is a Sources Sought notice issued by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) West, Network Contracting Office 17 (NCO 17), in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, Market Research. This notice is issued for information and market research purposes only. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), an Invitation for Bid (IFB), a Request for Quotation (RFQ), or an offer by the Government to contract for any supplies or services. This notice is not a commitment by the Government to award a contract, and the Government will not reimburse any respondent for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Responses to this notice are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right not to set aside this requirement or to otherwise change its acquisition strategy based on the results of this market research. 2. BACKGROUND AND DESCRIPTION OF THE REQUIREMENT The VA North Texas Health Care System (VANTHCS), Dallas VA Medical Center, requires the replacement of valves, gaskets, and vent lines on the main steam header and on Boilers 1, 2, and 3 located at the Energy Center, Building 70, 4500 S. Lancaster Road, Dallas, TX 75216. The existing valves are the original 1994 installation, and the age of the system has precluded effective maintenance and upkeep. Replacement valves and piping shall meet or exceed the specifications of the current installation and shall conform to applicable steam industry standards and regulations. The contractor shall provide all labor, supplies, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and management necessary to remove, purchase, install, and test the valves, gaskets, and vent lines on the main steam header and boilers. Key elements of the work include: Coordinating equipment shutdown with the facility representative / Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) prior to commencing work; Performing required lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures on affected equipment; Removing existing valves, vent lines, and associated components; Inspecting the interior of the main steam header body and checking the drip leg for blockages; Cleaning flange faces and installing new spiral-wound gaskets; Installing new steam valves with steam balancing and vent lines using Schedule 80 carbon steel piping and full-port ball valves (three-piece bolted, disassemble for internal component access without unthreading from the supply line); Installing new removable high-temperature insulation jackets on all steam valves; Replacing the boiler steam stop, isolation, and vent valves with new vent piping on Boilers 1, 2, and 3; and Performing leak checks, with the assistance of the COR and Utilities Systems Operator (USO), during boiler startup and campus pressurization to 110 psi. The Government anticipates a firm-fixed-price contract awarded under FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE VA North Texas Health Care System, Dallas VA Medical Center, Energy Center (Building 70), 4500 S. Lancaster Road, Dallas, TX 75216. 4. SDVOSB AND VOSB SET-ASIDE INTENT This requirement is anticipated to be set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) concerns in accordance with VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) Subpart 819.70, VA s VETS First Program, implemented under the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127(d) and 8127(e). This Sources Sought notice is issued in part to determine whether there are two or more responsible, capable SDVOSB or VOSB firms that can perform this requirement, and to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy. To be eligible for award under the anticipated set-aside, a firm must: Be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of response and award; Hold a current certification from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) as an SDVOSB or VOSB in accordance with 13 CFR Part 128; and Meet the small business size standard for NAICS code 238220 ($19.0 million average annual receipts). 5. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INTERESTED FIRMS Interested SDVOSB and VOSB firms are requested to submit a capability package that includes the following: Company Information: Legal business name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE code, physical and mailing addresses, website, and primary point of contact (name, title, telephone number, and email address); Business Status and Certifications: Small business size under NAICS 238220, SBA SDVOSB or VOSB certification status (including certification number and expiration date, if applicable), and any other socio-economic designations held; Relevant Experience: A description of comparable work performed within the past three (3) years involving steam distribution systems, steam headers, boiler plants, industrial piping, or similar mechanical/plumbing construction and maintenance. Include contract or task order numbers, the contracting activity or commercial customer, dollar value, period of performance, and whether the work was performed as a prime contractor or subcontractor; Technical Capability and Staffing: A description of the firm s capability, key personnel, and capacity to perform work of this type and magnitude at the Dallas VA Medical Center, including any applicable state of Texas licenses, welding certifications, or qualifications held by the firm or its personnel; Comments: Any comments or feedback regarding the scope of work, proposed NAICS code, anticipated contract structure, or other aspects of the planned acquisition. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS AND DEADLINE Responses must be submitted electronically via email to Ognian D. Ivanov, Contract Officer, at ognian.ivanov@va.gov . Use the following subject line: Sources Sought Steam Header and Boiler Valve Replacement [Company Name]. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 p.m. Central Time on November 9, 2026. Responses shall not exceed ten (10) pages in total (including all attachments) and shall be submitted in Microsoft Word or PDF format. Questions regarding this notice shall be submitted in writing via email to the point of contact listed above. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. Responses submitted after the deadline or to any other email address may not be considered. 7. IMPORTANT NOTICES This Sources Sought notice is issued solely for information, planning, and market research purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. title: Loaded Cartridge Assembly (MC91) for MK 5 Mod ) Explosive Bolt
description: This announcement should not be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Government. The U.S. Navy does not intend to award a contract based on this Request for Information/Sources Sought Notice. THIS IS NOT A Request for a Proposal AND DOES NOT OBLIGATE THE U.S. GOVERNMENT TO ISSUE an RFP. This RFI is for U.S. Government planning purposes only and constitutes requests for exchange of information pursuant to FAR Part 10. The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), Contracts Department, Code 02 is conducting Market Research on the Loaded Cartridge Assembly, DODIC MC91. NSWC IHD is conducting a market survey to identify sources/vendors capable of supplying the MC91 cartridge satisfying the following requirements: 1. The cartridge needs to meet the criteria specified by WS6061 and WS6052, ADL 2429839, their lower-tier documents, and be compatible with the MK 5 MOD 0 Explosive Bolt (M254), a critical component on the AN/BST-1 Buoy system. The Technical Data Package (TDP) contains technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act (Title 22, U.S.C., Sec 2751, et seq.). To receive the TDP, interested vendors must submit a written request accompanied by an approved DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement), signed NDA, and active CAGE code. 2. Contractor must be able to stand up a manufacturing line and be able to support the U.S. Government by providing all deliveries within one year of award. 3. Procurement includes production units (QTY 100) as well as all associated destructive test samples required for qualification and acceptance. This procurement includes the manufacture, testing (including nondestructive testing (NDT/radiographic) capabilities), packaging, and delivery of the MC91 Cartridge Assembly. Request your company provide responses to the following questionnaire: Does your company have a production line available that can meet the requirements mentioned above? If yes, describe your company's history and experience with supplying this item (or similar cartridges for explosive bolts) including the total number supplied to date and how the facilities are ready to support USG requirements. What is your company�s availability of inert metal parts or existing validated energetic loading lines? If the MC91 cartridges are not currently in stock, when would they be available for delivery? How many days or months after an award? Can your Company provide the rate of production the manufacturing facility is capable of per year? Can your company provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit price estimate based on the stated quantity of 100 production units plus required test samples, along with estimated stepped pricing for higher production rates? Do test reports exist that demonstrate the MC91 (or similar cartridges for explosive bolts) manufacturing accuracy and reliability? Actual reports are not required to be submitted as part of this request for information but will be accepted after your initial response to this request. Are you able to supply documented ability of your company's MC91 cartridges to function reliably with the MK 5 MOD 0 Explosive Bolt? Does your facility hold the necessary ATF licensing, Net Explosive Weight (NEW) storage capacity, and compliance with DoD 4145.26-M to manufacture, assemble, and store loaded MC91 cartridges? Describe your inspection capabilities for energetic components, specifically hermetic seal testing (helium leak rate) and real-time radiography (X-ray) for internal explosive pellet/column alignment. What are the lead times for primary energetic ingredients/mixes and specialized metal hardware required by WS6061 and WS6052? Are any materials obsolete or sole-sourced? Does your company possess or capability to produce all tooling, crimping dies, and electrical/bridgewire resistance test fixtures required to manufacture this item, or would Government-Furnished Equipment/Tooling (GFE/GFT) be required? Small Business Subcontracting & Nonmanufacturer Rule Compliance: If responding as a Small Business prime under NAICS 325920, please clarify your manufacturing approach: Does your company intend to perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding material costs) in-house at your own safety-approved facility? If you do not manufacture the cartridges in-house, do you intend to source the MC91 cartridges from another domestic small business manufacturer? If you intend to partner with a large business manufacturer, are you aware of the requirements to obtain an individual SBA Nonmanufacturer Rule (NMR) waiver prior to solicitation close? All interested sources shall provide the organization name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, business size, Unique Entity ID, and CAGE Code. In addition, all interested sources shall provide a summary of their company�s capabilities and delivery timeframe and schedule. All responding sources must email their response submissions no later than 17:00 Eastern Time on November 9, 2026 to the Point of Contacts (POCs) listed below. Submissions must be in PDF format and shall not exceed fifteen (15) pages in total. 1) NSWC IHD Attn: Michael Persinger Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806 Michael.a.persinger2.civ@us.navy.mil 2) NSWC IHD Attn: Gerardo Ilaria Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 gerardo.ilaria.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Notice of Opportunity (NOO) U.S. Army Reserve, 88th Readiness Division Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)
description: U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). These efforts align with statutory requirements under 10 U.S.C. � 2911 for energy security and resilience, and 42 U.S.C. � 8287 through the Department of Energy�s (DOE) Fourth-Generation Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. title: Notice of Opportunity (NOO) U.S. Army Reserve, 88th Readiness Division Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)
description: U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). These efforts align with statutory requirements under 10 U.S.C. � 2911 for energy security and resilience, and 42 U.S.C. � 8287 through the Department of Energy�s (DOE) Fourth-Generation Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Responses to this NOO must be received no later than 02 November, 3:00 p.m. (Ft. Belvoir, VA local time). Responses must be completed and submitted to the following email mailbox: DLAEnergy-ESPC@dla.mil

title: Notice of Opportunity (NOO) U.S. Army Reserve, 88th Readiness Division Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)
description: U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). These efforts align with statutory requirements under 10 U.S.C. � 2911 for energy security and resilience, and 42 U.S.C. � 8287 through the Department of Energy�s (DOE) Fourth-Generation Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Responses to this NOO must be received no later than 02 November, 3:00 p.m. (Ft. Belvoir, VA local time). Responses must be completed and submitted to the following email mailbox: DLAEnergy-ESPC@dla.mil

The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. description: The Government intends to hold a site visit for subject requirement on 4 November 2026 at 0900 AM. Below you will find the instructions and required documents to attend. Only SBA Certified Women Owned Small-Businesses are eligible for this requirement. **THIS IS THE ONLY DATE AND TIME FOR THE SITE VISIT, REQUESTS TO MAKE ANY CHANGES WILL BE DENIED** Attendance will be limited to 2 representatives for each contractor. To attend please provide the attached template (Site Visit Base Access_Template) completed with the below information, to rachel.tilley.1@us.af.mil, no later than 26 October 2026 at 1500 Arizona Time. Required Info: Last Name, First Name, DOB, US Citizen, License or ID#, State of Issue, Last 4 SSN To access the installation, the attendee will be required to have a REAL ID or Government Issued Passport. When submitting the above information, please include a copy of the form of ID to allow for Security Forces to verify if it meets the requirements. **QUESTIONS ARE DUE NO LATER THAN COB 22 OCTOBER 2026 at 1500 AZ time** ***FINALIZED Q&A Document will be posted with answers no later than 26 October 2026*** This SOW defines the requirement for the Contractor to Engineer, Furnish, Install and Test (EFI&T) new 12-Strand (St), Single Mode (SM) Fiber Optic Cable (FOC) from Radar Approach Control (RAPCON, B979) to Air Traffic Control Tower (ATCT, B998), Base Operation (Ops)B453), Command Post (CP, B11), Localizer (B1375), Glide Slope (GS, B1056), Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN, B1049), Ground Antenna Transmit and Receive (GATR, B1040), Glide Slope (B1081 and Localizer (B1059). Also, 12-St SM FOC from Base Ops (B453) to Primary and Secondary Automatic Meteorological Station (FMQ-19s). The work will be performed at Luke AFB AZ by using new and existing Manhole/Handhole Duct System. Some portion of the cable route/path will be Direct Buried. The Contractor shall provide all equipment, tools, materials, supplies, transportation, labor, supervision, management, and other incidentals necessary to meet the requirements as stated in this SOW. All equipment, supplies, or materials provided shall be new and not refurbished. No equipment, supplies, or material will be provided by the government. All materials used in this SOW must be rust-proof and corrosion-resistant, due to the nature of the environment. See attached Solicitation and supporting documents for additional information.

title: WSMR Tel Switch Support
description: The Range Operations Directorate at White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico is dedicated to having funcational and operational Nortel/Ribbon CS2100 and CS1000M switches range-wide, ensuring voice traffic is transported to its determined destination within Information Assurance and mission safety parameters. Currently their CS1000M and CS2100 are functional, but not operational because they depend on the connection to the STORM server. The STORM server is in fault mode and cannot provide the loading configurations to the CS1000M and CS2100. Contractor shall provide 24 hours, 7 days per week with a remote telephonic technical support license for an ESP Tier II and Ribbon Tier III license term of 12 months. When telephonic technical support is used, the issue will be resolved while on the phone with government personnel performing the fix. If the issue cannot be resolved, then on-site support will be required. The on-site support shall also include 3 site visits per year with each visit consisting of 24 hours at WSMR. To include on-site troubleshooting, diagnostics, routine technical assistance, and emergency technical assistance services as required. In addition to technical assistance, shall include testing, diagnostic fault isolation, problem resolution, and system restoration. Vendor must fix and retrieve the telephone switch files in the STORM Server, and clear possible faults on the CS1000M and CS2100. To include the possible replacement of the internal server hardware. Vendor must provide telephone support throughout the length of the service contract (1 year). The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is solely to gather preliminary information and explore potential solutions, capabilities, and approaches available in the market. title: NCTAMS PAC CAIRS Support
description: The Defense Information Systems Agency/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Unique Communications Solutions. A sole source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is for software access and continuous contracted maintenance support to keep Naval Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Station Pacific (NCTAMS PAC) subordinate sites Configuration Accounting Information Retrieval System (CAIRS) software packages current to meet JITC and IA security requirements in support of NCTAMS PAC regional BCO mission requirements. The current contract is in its fifth and final year. DITCO-PAC is establishing a new contract for one base year with four option periods. The consolidated contract supports Naval Computer and Telecommunications Station Far East (NCTS FE) to include Diego Garcia, NCTS Guam (NCTS GU), and NCTS San Diego (NCTS SD) and NCTS Detachment Puget Sound (NCTS PS). In Option Year One, services will include NCTAMS PAC in Wahiawa, Hawaii. The NCTAMS PAC Hawaii infrastructure is currently being installed and accredited at the estimated time of award and is not projected to need services/support until Q3/Q4 of 2027. At this time, the incumbent contractor Unique Communications Solutions is the only source capable of providing all necessary services for the NCTAMS PAC area of responsibility (AOR). Unique Communications Solutions is the sole OEM provider for the Configuration Accounting Information Retrieval System (CAIRS). The CAIRS system is unique in its functionality and features. There are no other companies that provide a system that has the exact components and abilities. CAIRS is trademarked through Unique Communications Solutions only. The Software Upgrade Kits are specific to the software they support. Unique Communications Solutions is the only company that can directly perform the following with the CAIRS programs: Upgrades, Update, Add Features, Fix Software problems, provide standard maintenance, Give training and technical support, Onsite Installation and Training. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 2304 (c) (1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1(c)(2), only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 5 days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Classification System (NAICS) code 541519 will be used for determining company size status. CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: Contract Number: HC1019-22-C-0004 Contract Type: Firm Fixed Price Incumbent and their size and CAGE: Unique Communications Solutions, Small Business, 0BBN7 Method of previous acquisition: Sole Source Period of performance: 26Sep2025 � 25Nov2026 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: None Points of Contact: jon.d.higgins2.civ@mail.mil

title: Construction Services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage St. Elizabeths West Campus
description: Amendment 0002 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0001 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. GSA anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price construction contract for the new construction of the Gate 7 Parking Garage and associated site, utility, security, stormwater, landscape, and infrastructure improvements. The project will support the operational needs of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. This acquisition is for construction services only. The project design is being completed separately by GSA�s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The work to be performed under the terms of this contract includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all management, supervision, subcontractors, labor, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, coordination, quality control, testing, inspections, commissioning support, and closeout documentation necessary to construct the Gate 7 Parking Garage in accordance with the contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior fa�ade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick fa�ade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. The estimated cost range for construction is between $120,000,000.00 and $160,000,000.00. The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Construction Concept. AMENDMENTS TO SOLICITATION: It is the offeror's responsibility to monitor SAM.gov for the release of any amendments. BONDING: A bid bond is required in Phase 2 as well as payment and performance bonds after award. SECURITY: Before employees are allowed to work under the anticipated contract, all personnel are required to pass a security check. Specific security requirements will be contained in the solicitation. FUNDS AVAILABILITY: Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government�s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. No legal liability on the part of the Government arises until award of the contract. ELIGIBLE OFFERORS: All responsible business firms may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. All prospective offerors are also required to use the System for Award Management at SAM.gov for registering their firm and completing representations and certifications. Any questions regarding this notification shall be directed to Jennifer Silkensen, Contracting Officer, via email at jennifer.silkensen@gsa.gov. Potential offerors are responsible for monitoring and downloading the solicitation and any potential amendments, if any, to the solicitation.

title: 56--PGMB Security Gate
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION TEMPLATE (FAR 12.603) General Information This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or services prepared in accordance with the format in subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 140RR027R0010 is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01. It is the responsibility of the contractor to be familiar with the applicable clauses and provisions. They may be accessed in full text at the following websites: https:/www.acquisition.gov/far/ and https://www.acquisition.gov/diar. This combined synopsis & solicitation notice is a request for competitive quotations. Therefore, all capability statements or quotations received prior to the RFQ close date will be considered. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 238990 with an associated small business size standard of $19M. Description of Services: The Department of Interior (BOR) require delivery date for an automated vehicular main entrance at the Pleasant Grove Office (PGMB)�capable of reliably controlling entry and exit and fully securing the existing driveway/entrance. Installation, testing, commissioning, and training shall be performed by the contractor at the Government�s destination. Statement of Objectives (SOO) 1. Purpose The purpose of this requirement is to provide an automated vehicular main entrance at the Pleasant Grove Office (PGMB) that reliably controls entry and exit and fully closes the existing driveway/entrance. The objective is to install a gate solution that integrates with the site's existing access-control infrastructure; card/badge readers and exit loop/coil, supports safe daily operations, and improves security. In addition to providing AHJ-approved emergency responder access at the new automated main entrance gate, the contractor shall standardize emergency responder access across the site by retrofitting two existing automated access gates with Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ)-approved emergency access key switches or equivalent devices. Each emergency access device shall be integrated with the respective gate operator control circuit to provide immediate emergency opening without replacement of Government access-control components and without defeating required gate safety functions. 2. Background The mission of the Bureau of Reclamation is to manage, develop, and protect water and related resources in an environmentally and economically sound manner in the interest of the American public. The mission of the Provo Area Office is to carry out this mission by supporting safe, reliable facility operations and daily activities at PGMB. This acquisition will deliver a complete gate solution that integrates with existing site infrastructure, including an existing electrical power source near the main entrance, installed card and badge readers for credentialed entry, and an existing loop/coil sensor that allows motor vehicles to exit the facility, and will standardize emergency responder access across all automated vehicular gates at PGMB. The main vehicular entrance is approximately forty feet (40 feet) wide. For planning purposes, the Government anticipates that approximately twenty-five feet (25 feet) of the entrance will be served by an automated vehicular gate, with approximately fifteen feet (15 feet) of chain-link infill tying into the existing fence line to close the remaining portion. These dimensions are approximate. Offerors shall verify field dimensions and site conditions and may propose the final gate configuration necessary to achieve the required security, access-control, safety, aesthetic, and operational outcomes. The current main entrance configuration has two individual gate leaves that are twenty feet (20 feet) each. To improve security and daily operations, the Government seeks a secure, access-controlled solution that closes the entrance and blends seamlessly with the existing chain-link fencing. For purposes of this requirement, security means controlling vehicular and personnel access to the facility, restricting unauthorized entry under normal operating conditions, maintaining reliable closure of the entrance, and integrating with the existing access control system. Existing Conditions and Key Constraints: � Aesthetic Continuity: Maintaining a clean, durable chain-link aesthetic that matches the existing fence visual continuity in pattern, alignment, and finish is required. � Height Matching: Matching the existing fence height at the tie-in location. � Access Integration: Integrating the new gate operator with the existing entry and exit access control system. � Safety and Reliability: Providing safe, reliable automation with entrapment protection, manual release, and commissioning proper operation. � Site Disruption: Minimize impact to staff, visitors, and ongoing site activities during installation. � Environmental Design: Designing the assembly for local wind and snow conditions. � Sustainability and Warranty: Provide maintainable equipment, warranty coverage, and Operations and Maintenance manuals. 3. Scope Offerors shall propose and furnish a complete entrance gate solution for the Bureau of Reclamation�s PGMB that achieves the outcomes identified in Section 4.0. The scope includes the overall management and integration of the work necessary to deliver a secure, access-controlled, automated entrance. Offerors will define their means and methods in their proposed Performance Work Statement. The solution shall close the existing entrance, which is approximately forty feet (40 feet) wide, using an automated vehicular gate solution serving approximately twenty-five feet (25 feet) of the entrance together with approximately fifteen feet (15 feet) of chain-link infill tying into the existing fence line, subject to field verification. Offerors shall determine the final dimensions, configuration, and means and methods necessary to achieve complete entrance closure. Integrate with the site's existing card and badge readers for credentialed entry and with the existing exit loop or coil sensor for automatic egress. Utilize the existing electrical power source, subject to field verification of voltage, circuit capacity, and suitability. Maintain a clean, durable chain-link aesthetic that matches or complements the existing fence and height; and support reliable daily operations under local wind and snow conditions while minimizing disruption during installation. The work shall include dismantling and removal of the existing main entrance gate leaves and associated hardware as required to install the new system. All removed gate materials shall be lawfully disposed of offsite. Existing fence, access-control components, utilities, and other features designated to remain shall be protected from damage. The new automated entrance gate shall include an AHJ-approved means of emergency responder access integrated with its gate operator. In addition, the contractor shall retrofit two existing automated access gates at PGMB with AHJ-approved emergency access key switches or equivalent devices. The emergency access work shall include all required interface components, wiring, conduit, labeling, enclosures, and mounting hardware. Each device shall be integrated directly with the respective gate operator control circuit to allow immediate opening by emergency responders while maintaining applicable UL 325 safety requirements. The contractor shall coordinate device type, mounting location, and installation details with the Fire Code Official and obtain all required approvals prior to installation.
